blogTitle: Officer's Notes (read before raid. All of it. I will know.)
about: Hello. I am Rick. I am 19. I lead a 40-man raiding guild called Overtime on a PvE server, and I run it from an Excel file named DKP_FINAL_v9_USE_THIS_ONE.xls. We raid Tuesday and Thursday at 8 PM server time. Doors close at 7:55. Raids end at 9:30 sharp. By day I am asleep. By night I work overnight stock at Price Plus #114, 10 PM to 6:30 AM, where I face the cereal aisle (I face it with care). People tell me I run raids like a shift manager. I do not see the problem. A raid is forty people who need to know where to stand, when their break is, and who is closing. We have reached Ragnaros nine times and killed him twice. Please be on time. Thank you.
aboutMore: A few things that are not in the rules. I say raids end at 9:30 because I clock in at 10. That is true. It is also when the fifteen-year-olds have to be in bed. I have never mentioned the second part and I would appreciate it if no one did. I have written six reference letters for guildies applying for real jobs. Four got the job. I round Kelly's DKP up. I know I am not supposed to. She works a double on Tuesdays and still shows up for the pull.
meet: Who I'd like to meet: Ragnaros, professionally. The man who invented the break room. Every healer who has ever stepped away mid-pull so I can say 'it is okay' (it is not okay, but I will say it). My manager Denise, to tell her I cannot come in on Thursday between 8 and 9:30 and see what she says (she will say 'ok'). Anyone who reads the guild rules to the end. There is a prize. It is nothing. But I will know.

interests.Movies: Apollo 13 (mission control is a raid leader with a headset), The Lord of the Rings (Helm's Deep is a 40-man where nobody stacked on the boss), Remember the Titans, Big Fish (my mother's pick), Cool Runnings (the team that just wants to finish)
interests.Television: Mythbusters (plan, test, explosion: a good raid structure), Dirty Jobs (the host respects the night shift and I respect the host), The Office (the American one) (I am not the boss, I relate to Stanley, who does crosswords through meetings), Antiques Roadshow (my mom's)
interests.Books: The Price Plus Employee Handbook, v14 (I have read all of it; the 'conflict resolution' section is just loot rules), The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People (my store manager's copy; I got to chapter 3, put first things first; I put raids first; he meant work), The Lord of the Rings, my own binder (it has tabs)
interests.Heroes: My mother (two jobs, never complains in front of me), Denise (shift manager, 11 years, zero missed days), Terry (our tank, 41, joined for his son, stayed for us), Kelly (our head healer, a nurse, works nights too), the person who first said 'ten minute break' and meant it

bulletins.subject: OVERTIME RAID RULES v9 (READ ALL OF IT) (I WILL KNOW)
bulletins.body: 1) Thank the healers. Out loud. 2) Doors close at 7:55. 3) Raid ends at 9:30. I clock in at 10. 4) Ten-minute break at the one hour mark. Bathroom, snack, stretch. You are not a machine. 5) No ninja looting. First offense: a talk. Second offense: a longer talk. Third offense: a binder. 6) Need before greed is a convention. Gary has explained this. 7) If you wipe, say 'my bad.' Nobody has ever been fired for 'my bad.' 8) If someone else wipes, say 'we got it next time.' 9) If you are late, say so FIRST. Late and honest beats on time and silent. 10) Thank the healers again. That is the whole rule. The other nine are details.

dms: malten. 3 AM. Aisle 14. A customer asked me where the cereal was. I was facing the cereal. I pointed at it. She looked at me for a while and said 'You look tired.' I said 'I raid on Thursdays.' She said 'That sounds nice.' It does. It does sound nice. I thought you should know that somebody said that to me.

My mother works two jobs and I work one and a half (the half is the guild). She asked what the guild does. I said 'We kill a fire monster.' She said 'For money?' I said 'For loot.' She asked what it was worth. I said 'Nothing.' She said 'Then why are you tired.' I said 'It is the people.' She nodded like that was an answer. It was. I wrote it down.

I wrote a reference letter for a guildie today. She is 16 and applying to a bowling alley. The letter says 'Priya has never been late, and when she is late, she says so first.' I have never written anything that fast. I am putting it in the guild handbook under 'Being a Person.'
We wiped 11 times on Garr tonight. I said 'Good attempt.' Forty people said 'Thanks, Rick.' Nobody has ever thanked me for something I did badly. Something is wrong with these people. I love them.

I made Dave IT officer. He is 16. His only job is to tell me when Ventrilo is down. It has been down three times. He told me each time, correctly, within seconds. Best IT officer I have ever had. Only IT officer I have ever had.

Someone left a plate of cookies in the break room with a note: 'For the night crew.' We ate 22 cookies in nine minutes. I wrote 'thank you' on a post-it. Someone wrote back 'It is what we do.' I have been smiling since 4 AM and nobody in aisle 14 knows why.

Our tank, Terry, is 41. He is a dad. He joined the raid because his son plays and he wanted to know what the fuss was. His son quit. Terry stayed. Last night he asked me, very quietly, if he is 'doing it right.' I said, 'Terry, you are the reason we are doing it at all.' He did not say anything. Then he said 'Pull.'

My shift manager Denise has not missed a day in eleven years. I asked her how. She said, 'You just show up and then you are there.' I asked what happens when you do not feel like it. She said, 'That is what the first hour is for.' I have used this to run a raid six times.

blog.title: How I Run a 40-Man Raid (a manager's guide)
blog.body: People ask how one nineteen-year-old runs forty people. Here is the whole system. ONE: write the schedule down and never change it. Forty people can survive a bad plan if the plan is stable. TWO: give each person one job and say it out loud. 'Terry, you hold the boss. Kelly, you keep Terry up.' People relax when they know where to stand. THREE: break at the hour mark. Ten minutes. Nobody does good work without a break and I learned that at a register. FOUR: thank the healers. FIVE: when something goes wrong, say 'we got it next time' before anyone else says anything. The first sentence after a wipe is the whole raid. SIX: end on time. Always. People will follow you into a fire if you promise to get them out by 9:30.

blog.title: I Wrote A Reference Letter
blog.body: A guildie of mine, 16, asked me to be a reference for a job at a bowling alley. She has never had a job. She said 'I do not know anyone who would say anything about me.' I said I would. I sat in the break room at 4 AM and drafted it on the back of a delivery slip. It said: To Whom It May Concern, I have worked with Priya for fourteen months. She has never been late, and when she is late, she tells me first. She has never been rude to a teammate, including the ones who deserved it. She stays for the last pull even when she has a test. I would trust her with a key. Sincerely, Rick Alvarez, Night Operations. She got the job. She sent me a picture of her name tag. I printed it. It is in my locker next to the schedule. That makes six letters. Four got the job.

blog.title: 3:07 AM, Aisle 14 (a short one)
blog.body: The store is empty at 3 AM. The lights hum. There is a certain kind of quiet that only happens when you are the only person awake in a building made for four hundred. I face the cereal. You pull each box to the front edge of the shelf so the aisle looks full. It is a small thing. In the morning a woman will walk down this aisle, see a full shelf, and not think about it. That is the job. You do something at 3 AM so a stranger does not have to think about it at 9. I think about that during raids. I think the healers know it too. Nobody sees what they do and everything works because of it. At 3:07 I stop and read the guild chat I missed. Someone wrote 'GN everyone.' Six people wrote it back. I wrote it too. I was at work. It was fine.

qa: Name / character name:
Rick Alvarez / Rickard (a dwarf warrior; it was going to be Richard but the name was taken)
Class and role:
Warrior. Officer. The guy next to the tank who tells him where to stand.
Availability:
Tuesday and Thursday, 8 PM server. Raid ends 9:30 sharp. I clock in at 10.
Attendance record:
Fourteen months. Zero missed raids. Two late. I said so first.
What do you do when a boss wipes the raid?
Say 'we got it next time.' Then I check on the healer.
Thoughts on ninja looting:
I have a binder. It is 4 pages. Page 1 says 'No.'
References:
Denise (shift manager, 11 years, never missed a day). Terry (tank, 41). A girl named Priya who works at a bowling alley now.
Why Overtime?
Because everyone is already tired. We might as well be tired together.
How many break minutes do you need?
Ten. It is the best ten minutes of a raid. I will not move it.
Favorite thing about the job:
The moment right before the pull when nobody is talking and everyone is in position.
Least favorite thing:
The moment right after a wipe when someone says 'sorry.' Nobody has to be sorry. I will say so.
Anything else we should know:
The vending machine at work has a row that does not drop. I tell you so you know I do not give up on things easily.
